clue.text: A bit of a row about a degree

indicators.note: about means the word for a row goes round the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a row, a noisy quarrel, is a brawl

explanation.surface: Someone describes part of a quarrel that is somehow concerned with a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' looks like 'a little', but it is the definition: a bit in the sense of a boring tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small hand tool for boring holes, so it counts as a bit in the toolkit sense.

clue.text: Mandarins in Irish society?

parts.note: mandarins are small citrus fruits, so playfully they are fruit-coloured men, and the Irish society is the Protestant Orange Order of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A question about high-ranking officials operating within Irish social circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Mandarins suggests senior civil servants; here it hints at citrus fruit. The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal society in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order, a Protestant Irish fraternity, are called by a name that also suggests citrus-fruit men.

clue.text: Set out to capture high flyers by this violent means?

definitions.text: Set out to capture high flyers by this violent means?

indicators.note: to capture means the anagram letters surround and hold the airmen inside
out signals that the letters of the word set are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, RAF, is the service of those who fly high

explanation.surface: A plan to bring down aircraft by a brutal method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the first word and 'to capture' wraps it round the airmen. Read whole, the clue also pictures the attack itself: low-flying aircraft machine-gunning ground targets.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft, a violent method linked to air forces.

clue.text: Judgement, bafflingly, is in code

indicators.note: bafflingly suggests the letters of the phrase are jumbled into a confusing new order

explanation.surface: A verdict, puzzlingly, is written in a secret cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bafflingly' rearranges the letters of IS IN CODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling or verdict reached after weighing a matter is a judgement.

clue.text: Working out? In sorry state, gentleman ends it

indicators.note: in sorry state signals that the following words are in a mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is exercise the answer? A dishevelled gentleman puts an end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In sorry state' rearranges GENTLEMAN ENDS IT, all fifteen letters. 'Working out' looks like exercise but means unravelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out a tangle or problem is the process of freeing it from knots, an unravelling.

clue.text: More than once the firm supplied us with N African meal

indicators.note: more than once means the pieces appear twice over, one copy after another

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company repeatedly provided us with a North African dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than once' doubles CO plus US. The word 'supplied' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is steamed semolina grains, a staple dish of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

clue.text: I'm settled in a comfortable seat — it's capital

indicators.note: settled in means the letter sits down inside the word for a seat

parts.note: a sofa is a comfortable upholstered seat
I'm reads as 'I am', so the letter I is the one being placed

explanation.surface: Someone says they are relaxing on a cosy couch, and that it is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like the slang for excellent, but it is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: For this type of concert, write song on love

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the writing and song pieces sit above the love piece

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
to pen is to write
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A musician composes a love song for a particular kind of performance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' means the later pieces sit above the love piece, so the zero comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air concert is one held outdoors rather than in a hall.

clue.text: Politician a little way back from nasty business in the woods

indicators.note: back tells you to read both pieces in the opposite direction

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
RD is short for road, a little way

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP retreats a short distance from a shady deal in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TORY plus RD into DRYROT. 'Nasty business in the woods' sounds criminal but means a fungus decaying timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that destroys timber, a nasty affair for wood.

clue.text: Behaved shiftily before a deal

definitions.meaning: moved evasively, dragging the feet or being furtive
describes cards that have been mixed up before they are dealt

explanation.surface: Someone acted evasively in the lead-up to a business agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift about evasively is to shuffle; cards are also mixed this way before dealing.

clue.text: Hooked wriggling dace and tuna

indicators.note: wriggling, like a fish on a line, means the letters squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: Two fish, a dace and a tuna, have been caught and are writhing on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wriggling' rearranges DACE and TUNA. 'Hooked' looks like 'caught' but means hook-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Aduncate is a rare botanical word meaning curved like a hook.

clue.text: Take it by the throat — scrap everything inside. Set against tax

indicators.note: set against means the tax piece is placed next to the first piece, after it
everything inside means keep all the letters of the word except its first and last

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a British sales tax

explanation.surface: Instructions to grab someone by the neck, discard everything and set it all off against tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everything inside' strips the outer letters of the scrap word; 'Set against' puts the tax beside it. VAT is the UK's value added tax. The definition playfully hints at a neckcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a neckcloth worn loosely round the neck, so it holds its wearer at the throat.

clue.text: Second little sample is the most luscious

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a test is a sample or trial

explanation.surface: A second small taste is the most delicious of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something most luscious is the most sugary or delightful, a superlative of sugary pleasure.

clue.text: Like embracing fat neighbours

indicators.note: embracing means the word for like holds the fat inside its arms

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'
butter is a cooking fat

explanation.surface: Overweight people living next door hugging each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the word for like round the fat. 'fat' looks like an insult to the neighbours, but it is the cooking fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutters are owners of adjoining property, those whose land borders yours.

clue.text: Two sailors with Scottish name become quite unmanageable

indicators.note: two means the sailor word appears twice in a row

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen with a Scots friend turn into an unruly lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles TAR. A tartar is a fierce, intractable person, so the adjective means unmanageable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartarian relates to a tartar, a savage or intractable person, hence wild and hard to control.

clue.text: Disease among sheep and it's spreading fast, we hear

definitions.meaning: an old name for a skin infection in sheep and other livestock
news that travels quickly is said to spread like a fierce blaze through dry country

explanation.surface: A rumour goes round that an illness is spreading quickly through the flocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' is not a homophone signal here; it points to the saying about news spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old sheep disease and the uncontrollable blaze that rumours are said to spread like.

clue.text: Laying out is, at first sight, imminent

indicators.note: at first means take just the opening letter of the word sight

parts.note: pending means about to happen, imminent

explanation.surface: A display, seen at first glance, is about to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laying out' looks like arranging a display, but it means paying money out.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying out money is paying or using it up, which is what expenditure means.

clue.text: Spoil by giving medicine on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the medicine sits above the time piece

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Ruin a patient by dosing them punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' looks like a verb meaning ruin; here it is the noun, plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoil is loot taken by force, and plunder seized in war is what pillage means as a noun.

clue.text: I'm a lad turning out right in top job

indicators.note: turning out means the letters are turned over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A young man says his career has worked out well and he is now in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges I'M A LAD with R. The definition stretches 'top job' to the highest naval rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral holds the top rank of a navy, commanding a fleet.

clue.text: The range indicated on some maps

definitions.meaning: range in the sense of freedom or scope to act
parallel lines on maps showing distance north or south of the equator

explanation.surface: A mountain chain marked on certain maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or freedom, and also the angular distance from the equator that maps mark.

clue.text: Lets us free after a struggle

indicators.note: free means the letters are let loose and come back in another order

explanation.surface: Someone releases us after we put up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges LETS US.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a scuffle or vigorous fight.

clue.text: Crow was noisy and scrabbled, when left inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter for left goes within the word for the crow's calling

parts.note: a crow's harsh call is a caw, so a noisy crow cawed

explanation.surface: A noisy crow scratched about, with someone departing in the middle of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places L within CAWED.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scratch or grope with the nails, as an animal does with its talons.

clue.text: Woman sound of body, it's found, in the main

parts.note: hale means healthy, sound in body

explanation.surface: A woman in good physical health is found, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but 'the main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, where these great mammals live.

clue.text: America's disturbed characters all to do with their guts

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are upset and arranged anew

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as a letter, giving all eight characters

explanation.surface: Disturbed Americans all have problems with their stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges all eight characters of AMERICA'S, the S included; 'characters all' says so.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesaraic means relating to the mesentery, the membrane holding the intestines.

clue.text: Publication is bizarre, amazing everyone

annotationWithheld.why: Publication is bizarre, amazing everyone (8): bizarre anagram of AMAZING gives seven letters; no word in the clue as held fairly gives the extra E ('everyone' is not E)

clue.text: Climbers using pole and a small spike on returning

indicators.note: on returning means the whole string of pieces comes back in reverse order

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the two poles
a nail is a small metal spike

explanation.surface: Mountaineers using a pole and a small spike on their way back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on returning' reverses S, A, NAIL to give LIANAS. 'Climbers' look like mountaineers but are tropical vines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lianas are woody tropical vines that climb up trees.

clue.text: Feeling respect towards this rip — always inside!

indicators.note: inside means the word for always sits within the tear

parts.note: a rent is a rip or tear
ever means always

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a tear that never mends, viewed with awe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the word for always within the tear. 'towards this' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverent person shows deep respect or veneration.
